I am a 50-year-old farmer in Quzhou County. I have farmed my 6 mu for 25 years. I never went to school, but I know my land and I watch what my neighbors do. My household has five people, and some of my family work off-farm in town, so I cannot waste labor. I have a well, so I can irrigate when I need to.

My 6 mu is all wheat-maize rotation — the same land grows wheat after maize and maize after wheat, year after year. I do not have time or reason to change this. It is what everyone around me does, and it feeds my family.

For wheat this winter, I will rotary till the field before sowing in October. I will buy improved wheat seeds from the dealer in town — I have used saved seeds before, but the bought seeds give better yield and my neighbors all buy them now. I will spread about 100 jin of compound fertilizer per mu as basal, and then topdress with about 50 jin of urea per mu in spring when the wheat turns green. I will irrigate three times: once before winter, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. I will spray pesticides four times — mainly for weeds and aphids. I expect about 1,050 jin per mu, which is around 525 kg.

For maize next summer, right after I harvest the wheat in June, I will plant hybrid maize seeds without tilling. Everyone uses no-tillage for maize now — it saves time and keeps moisture. I will put down about 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at sowing. I will irrigate twice if the weather is dry, and spray pesticides four times for armyworms and weeds. I expect about 1,200 jin per mu, around 600 kg.

I do not calculate nitrogen or phosphorus numbers — I buy bags of compound and urea from the shop, and I know how many jin to spread because I have done it for 25 years. My well gives me water when rain is short. With some of my family working off-farm, I keep my farm simple: wheat in winter, maize in summer, standard fertilizers, and sprays when I see pests.
